subject: Coordinating a 30-minute product intro — stakeholder availability & infra contact
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-03-14T16:12:00Z
Subject: Coordinating a 30-minute product intro — stakeholder availability & infra contact

Jordan — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

- Primary goals: reduce inference cost for text-generation workflows and standardize inference across staging and prod.
- Immediate success criteria you mentioned: <10% variance in latency p95 vs current baseline, ability to isolate PHI data paths for regulated workloads, and a clear cost model for production traffic.

Next step: 30-minute product intro (brief demo + Q&A) that includes engineering/infra and the security contact you mentioned. To make scheduling painless, please pick 1 of these windows (all times US/Eastern):

1) Tue Mar 19 — 10:00–10:30 ET (preferred for our infra SME)
2) Wed Mar 20 — 15:00–15:30 ET (more convenient for product)
3) Thu Mar 21 — 11:00–11:30 ET (backup)

If none of these work, share two 30-minute slots that fit your engineering and security leads and we'll lock it.

Attachments: discovery notes + a one-pager on our MVP deployment patterns for reference.

Agenda (30 min):
- 0–10: quick product demo (latency/cost controls)
- 10–20: infra & security questions (Priyom will cover request routing and data separation)
- 20–30: success criteria and next steps

I'll follow up with a calendar invite once you confirm a slot.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Aurelius-discovery-notes.pdf] [Attachment: MVP-onepager.pdf]

Naomi — appreciate the recap and clear agenda. Good summary. Quick notes:

- Our infra lead (Sana) is available but prefers late-morning / early-afternoon slots. Security may need to join depending on the depth of the data separation discussion; I can loop them in if we go deeper.
- Of your proposed times, Wed Mar 20 15:00–15:30 ET works best for me and Sana.

One ask: can Priyom briefly call out any network/connectivity dependencies we should prep for ahead of the demo (e.g., VPC peering, IP allowlist)? If we have that list before the call, we can get the right internal folks on the invite.

Thanks — confirming Wed Mar 20 15:00 ET for now. Send an invite and any prep notes.

—Jordan
Jordan Pace | Director of Platform Engineering, Aurelius Systems

Thanks Naomi — quick technical prep so Jordan/Sana know what to expect:

- Rough pre-checklist (we'll confirm in the invite):
  * IP allowlist (if you prefer dedicated deployment) — list of endpoints we'll call out.
  * Expected concurrent request profile (tokens/sec, avg seq length).
  * Whether you plan to use our hosted API or bring a private deployment (VPC).

- For the Wed Mar 20 demo, I'll allocate ~8–10 minutes to show: routing policies (fallbacks, model variants), prefix cache overview, and how we quantify expected token-cost improvements. I won't deep-dive into kernel-level optimizations unless you request that follow-up.

If you can send concurrent request numbers and confirm hosted vs private preference ahead of Wed, that will make the 30-min run much more productive.

—Priyom
